  •  Middle Childhood (6–12 yrs) – Social and academic growth
  •  Adolescence (12–18 yrs) – Identity formation and emotional changes
  •  Adulthood (18+ yrs) – Responsibilities, relationships, and career

questions.question: Analyze the importance of Piaget’s cognitive stages in understanding the / behaviour of a child.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the importance of Piaget’s cognitive stages in understanding the behavior of a child.
  • Jean Piaget proposed that children develop through four cognitive stages.
  •  Helps understand how children think differently from adults, not just less intelligently.
  •  Sensor motor stage (0–2 yrs) explains learning through senses and object permanence.
  • marks
  •  Preoperational stage (2–7 yrs) highlights egocentrism and symbolic thinking.
  •  Concrete operational stage (7–11 yrs) shows logical thinking about concrete objects.
  •  Formal operational stage (11+ yrs) explains abstract and hypothetical thinking.
  •  Assists teachers and social workers in designing age-appropriate interventions.
  •  Helps explain behavioral limitations, such as inability to understand others’ perspectives.
  •  Useful in identifying developmental delays or cognitive impairments.
  •  Supports effective communication by aligning with the child’s level of understanding.
questions.final_answer:  Supports effective communication by aligning with the child’s level of understanding

questions.question: Analyze the impact of group behaviour on individual identity.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the impact of group behavior on individual identity.
  •  Group behavior strongly shapes individual beliefs, values, and attitudes.
  •  Individuals often conform due to social pressure . (10 marks)
  •  The theory of social identity was developed by Henri Tajfel.
  •  Group membership gives a sense of belonging and self-esteem.
  •  Peer groups significantly influence behavior, especially during adolescence.
  •  Can lead to positive outcomes like cooperation, teamwork, and social support.
  •  May also result in negative effects like peer pressure, groupthink, or loss of individuality.
  •  Individuals may change behavior to match group norms and expectations.
  •  Group identity can influence decision-making and moral judgments.
  •  Understanding group behavior helps social workers manage group dynamics and interventions
  • effectively.
